blocks.text: Salesforce Data Cloud Suite is a Discovery-phase toolkit that pairs a Credit Consumption Analyser (cost estimation) with a Data Readiness Validator (source-system quality checks).

items: Credit Consumption Analyser: models one-time Initial Load and ongoing Incremental annual cost using the official Salesforce Data Cloud Platform Services Rate Sheet.
Data Readiness Validator: connects to Salesforce/Zendesk/SharePoint and runs configurable duplicate checks against selected object-field combinations.

blocks.text: All calculations run in-browser; only external API calls are proxied through the Next.js server.

blocks.content:
Initial Credits    = (units / unitDivisor) * creditsPerUnit
Annual Credits     = (unitsPerDay / unitDivisor) * creditsPerUnit * runsPerDay * daysPerYear

Both are then multiplied by:
  envMultiplier   (1.0 for Production, 0.8 for Sandbox by default)
  (1 + overheadPct) (default 10%)

Cost USD          = Credits * costPerCreditUSD ($0.005 by default)
Grand Total       = (splitInitialLoad ? initialCost : 0) + incrementalAnnualCost

rows: External Batch/Streaming Ingestion, Transforms, Data Federation, Data Share, Private Connect, Unstructured Data
Segment Rows Processed, Batch Activation, Streaming Activation

blocks.content:
Scenario: External Batch Ingestion, 150,000 rows/day, Production, 10% overhead

Annual credits = (150,000 / 1,000,000) * 2,000 * 1 * 365 = 109,500 cr
With envMul 1.0 and overhead 1.10:
Final credits = 109,500 * 1.10 = 120,450 cr
Cost          = 120,450 * $0.005 = $602.25 / year

items: Select System - Salesforce, Zendesk, or SharePoint.
Connection - enter credentials; optionally save with masked passwords; Test Connection validates auth.
Objects - metadata is fetched live; pick which objects to short-list.
Configure Rules - build one or more rules combining Validation Type + Object + Field + Threshold; field dropdown is dependent on object.
Run - execute all rules on the backend with live logs.
Results - per-rule table, overall score, recommendations, exportable PDF.

blocks.text: Older versions used SELECT ... GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT > 1 LIMIT 200. Salesforce caps this at 200 rows and forbids removing the limit (EXCEEDED_ID_LIMIT). If a table had more than 200 duplicate groups, the counted duplicate rate was severely under-reported (e.g. 0.08% instead of the real 86%).
v3.4 switches Salesforce to COUNT_DISTINCT which is a server-side aggregation returning a single number and is NOT subject to the 200-row cap.

blocks.content:
SALESFORCE (v3.4 accurate):
  Q1: SELECT COUNT() FROM {object}                                    -- totalCount
  Q2: SELECT COUNT() FROM {object} WHERE {field} != null              -- nonNullCount
  Q3: SELECT COUNT_DISTINCT({field}) v FROM {object}
      WHERE {field} != null                                            -- uniqueValues (EXACT)

  duplicateExtras = nonNullCount - uniqueValues     -- ALWAYS ACCURATE
  duplicateRate   = duplicateExtras / nonNullCount

  Q4 (optional, for display only): SELECT {field}, COUNT(Id) c FROM {object}
      WHERE {field} != null GROUP BY {field} HAVING COUNT(Id) > 1
      ORDER BY COUNT(Id) DESC LIMIT 200               -- top 5 shown as sample

ZENDESK:
  Paginate up to 5 pages of 100 records; count occurrences in-memory.
  duplicateExtras = sampled - uniqueValuesInSample
  duplicateRate   = duplicateExtras / sampled
  method          = sampled-paginated (5 pages max)

SHAREPOINT:
  Fetch up to 1,000 list items via Graph with $expand=fields.
  duplicateExtras = itemCount - uniqueValuesInSample
  duplicateRate   = duplicateExtras / itemCount
  method          = listing-1000-items

score  = max(0, 100 - round(duplicateRate * 400))
status = pass  if pct <= threshold
         warn  if pct <= 2 * threshold
         fail  otherwise

overallScore  = average of all rule scores
overallRating = Ready      (>= 80)
                Needs Work (>= 60)
                At Risk    (else)

blocks.text: Zendesk and SharePoint counts are sample-based due to API limits. For definitive numbers on very large datasets, run an offline export. Salesforce counts are exact.
All endpoints are POST-only, run on the Node.js runtime, and return {logs: LogEntry[]} in every response so the UI can render a live console.

rows: Run one or more duplicate rules

items: INFO - milestone / result (slate)
HTTP - outbound HTTP call (cyan)
SOQL - Salesforce query (purple)
WARN - non-fatal (amber)
ERROR - failure (red)
Credentials are POSTed once per request to the Next.js server; nothing is persisted server-side.
Saved Connections live in browser localStorage only; passwords are shown masked as ab***yz.
Log sanitiser redacts any key containing password, apiToken, clientSecret, securityToken, authorization, or sessionId before logs leave the server.
All duplicate-check queries are read-only. No writes ever occur on the source system.

blocks.text: For production usage, replace lib/connections.ts with a server-side encrypted store rather than localStorage.
